overview: The Ministry of Road Transport & Highways (MoRTH) has announced opportunities for startups and private entities to participate in Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) toll highway projects under Public-Private Partnership (PPP) models. These opportunities involve Design, Build, Finance, Operate, and Transfer (DBFOT) models for national highway projects, enabling private sector participation in infrastructure development through toll revenue collection.
objectives: Promote private sector participation in national highway development
Develop highway infrastructure through PPP models like DBFOT and BOT (Toll)
Ensure efficient financing, construction, operation, and maintenance of highway projects
Facilitate toll-based revenue generation for project sustainability
Improve connectivity and reduce logistics costs through enhanced road infrastructure
Encourage innovation in highway construction and maintenance through private sector efficiency
Ensure timely completion and quality adherence in highway projects
eligibility: Private companies, consortia, or special purpose vehicles (SPVs) registered under the Companies Act, 2013 or relevant statutes, with demonstrated technical and financial capacity to undertake highway projects on DBFOT or BOT (Toll) basis, meeting pre-qualification criteria set by MoRTH or NHAI for specific projects.
benefits: Opportunity to develop and operate national highway projects on DBFOT/BOT (Toll) basis, earn revenue through toll collection over concession period, contribute to national infrastructure development, avail tax benefits and incentives under PPP frameworks, and gain long-term operational rights over developed assets.
financial_support: Financial support is not provided as a grant or subsidy; instead, private entities are responsible for financing the project through equity and debt. Revenue is generated through toll collection during the concession period, with financial closure required as part of the bid process.
application_process: 1. Identify upcoming BOT (Toll) highway projects announced by MoRTH or NHAI. 2. Check eligibility and pre-qualification criteria published in the project RFP. 3. Prepare and submit bid documents including technical and financial proposals. 4. Submit bid through the designated portal (e.g., NHAI e-tendering portal) before the deadline. 5. Participate in bid opening and evaluation process. 6. If selected, sign the concession agreement and achieve financial closure. 7. Proceed with land acquisition, clearances, and construction as per agreement.
required_documents: Audited financial statements of the last 3 years
Details of promoter and shareholding structure
Technical bid with project methodology and work plan
Financial bid with tolling and financing plan
Power of attorney and board resolution
deadlines: Project-specific; varies per tender. Bids must be submitted before the deadline specified in the individual project's Request for Proposal (RFP).
implementing_agency: Ministry of Road Transport & Highways (MoRTH), Government of India
contact_details: Email: planningmorth@gmail.com | Helpline: Not explicitly mentioned in evidence
caveats: Projects are awarded through competitive bidding; selection is not guaranteed
Private entity bears all financial risks including cost overruns and revenue shortfalls
Concession period is fixed; asset reverts to government after concession period
Compliance with environmental, land acquisition, and statutory clearances is mandatory
Toll rates may be subject to regulation or caps as per government policy
